notes: Positive: prompts where the user asks for system-level design, NFRs, ADRs, C4, modernization strategy, or technology choice WITHOUT requesting implementation. Negative: implementation-only, code review, test strategy, security-only, infra provisioning, or meta-skill component edits. Edge: ambiguous between design and implementation, or where the user asks 'how should I' without naming code.

cases.query: Design the architecture for a multi-tenant SaaS billing engine — bounded contexts, data model at the conceptual level, API boundaries, NFRs with concrete targets, and ADRs for the major decisions
We have a monolith we want to break up — evaluate strangler-fig vs branch-by-abstraction vs big rewrite, identify the bounded-context seams, and propose a phased migration with rollback at each phase

Should we use Postgres or DynamoDB for the orders service? Walk me through the trade-offs against our NFRs (p95 < 80 ms at 5k RPS, strong consistency on the order line items, multi-region read traffic)
Draw the C4 Context and Container diagrams for our checkout pipeline and propose ADRs for the asynchronous integration with the warehouse system
Define the NFRs (latency, availability, durability, recoverability, cost) for the new fraud-detection service so the team can start engineering against concrete targets
Compare REST vs gRPC vs GraphQL for our public partner API given the consumer profile (six SaaS partners, mostly read-heavy, occasional bulk export). Recommend with the trade-off, not the conclusion

We want to add event-driven flows between order, inventory, and shipping — propose the integration pattern (saga vs choreography vs outbox), data ownership boundaries, and how we keep things idempotent
Define fitness functions for our service so the architecture does not drift: performance, modularity (dependency direction), maintainability (complexity), and cost per transaction
Write the ADR for our decision to move from Kafka to NATS JetStream — context, decision, consequences (positive and negative), and the rollback we accept

How should we structure a modular monolith for our marketplace product so we can extract services later when bounded contexts stabilize — propose module boundaries, dependency rules, and the seam strategy
Implement the order-cancellation endpoint in our Express service
Review this PR and tell me if it looks safe to merge
Design the test pyramid for our payments service
Threat-model the checkout service using STRIDE
cases.notes: Threat modeling is security work, not architecture work.
